anomalies.description: A large, violent explosion originates from a compound near a canal and highway, producing an intense fireball followed by a rapidly expanding mushroom-shaped plume of smoke and debris. The blast fully engulfs the structure and propagates outward over ~6.5 seconds.
A large, violent explosion originates from a ground structure, rapidly expanding into a fireball and then a massive mushrooming plume of smoke and debris over ~7.5 seconds.

A large, violent explosion occurs at ground level, producing a rapidly expanding fireball and a massive plume of dense gray and black smoke that rises and billows upward, obscuring the site. The initial blast is visible in f0–f3, with peak expansion and smoke column development through f4–f6.

A secondary, smaller explosion or intense combustion event occurs as the main smoke cloud begins to dissipate; visible as a localized bright flash and renewed dark smoke surge near the ground in the lower right portion of the frame.

A large, sudden detonation occurs at ground level, producing an intense fireball and a rapidly expanding plume of dark smoke and debris, characteristic of a high-energy explosion.; Secondary explosions or continued violent combustion are visible as the smoke column surges upward and outward with significant force, indicating ongoing explosive activity in the immediate aftermath of the initial blast.
